title: BBC Learning English from the News 2024 — Quiz 4
description: Choose the best answer for each question about vocabulary and usage.

elements.name: q31_godfather_of
elements.title: A critic calls a musician “the godfather of modern jazz drumming”. What is the critic suggesting?
choices: He helped develop and shape that style.
He dislikes that style of music.
He was the youngest drummer to play it.
He learned the style later in his career.
elements.correctAnswer: He helped develop and shape that style.

elements.name: q32_dubbed
elements.title: The press dubbed the small robot “the Pocket Helper”. What did the press do?
choices: Published its instruction manual
Translated the manufacturer's name
Gave it a nickname
Announced a release date

elements.name: q33_doomsayer
elements.title: Who would most likely be called a doomsayer?
choices: Someone who keeps predicting disastrous outcomes
Someone who refuses to make predictions
Someone who is confident things will improve
Someone who keeps a record of past events
elements.correctAnswer: Someone who keeps predicting disastrous outcomes

elements.name: q34_pay_for
elements.title: “The firm paid for ignoring customers' complaints when sales fell.” What does “paid for” mean here?
choices: Suffered the consequences of
Received an invoice for
Set aside money for
Gave a refund for

elements.name: q35_flex_its_muscles
elements.title: “The company flexed its muscles by showing competitors how much it could produce.” What does the phrase mean?
choices: Hid its production capacity
Sought help from competitors
Gave up its advantages
Showed how powerful it was

elements.name: q36_offensive
elements.title: A report calls a series of coordinated military operations an offensive. What does “offensive” mean here?
choices: An agreement to stop fighting
A planned military campaign
A line marking a national border
An insult directed at someone

elements.name: q37_toxic
elements.title: Employees described the workplace as toxic. What are they suggesting?
choices: The environment harmed their well-being over time.
The work required specialist training.
The office was hard to reach.
The workplace had an unusual opening schedule.
elements.correctAnswer: The environment harmed their well-being over time.

elements.name: q38_on_the_cusp_of
elements.title: “The team is on the cusp of a breakthrough.” What does this mean?
choices: A breakthrough has already been announced.
A breakthrough happened years ago.
A breakthrough was ruled out.
A breakthrough is about to happen.
elements.correctAnswer: A breakthrough is about to happen.

elements.name: q39_shocker
elements.title: “The bus is late again. Shocker.” If the speaker is being sarcastic, what do they mean?
choices: They are genuinely astonished.
They doubt the bus is late.
They think the bus came early.
They expected the bus to be late.
elements.correctAnswer: They expected the bus to be late.

elements.name: q40_braces_for
elements.title: The town braces for a flood by putting out sandbags. What does it do?
choices: Checks the damage after the flood
Signals that the flood has passed
Studies the cause of a previous flood
Prepares for the flood
